question.text: Based on the angles shown in the figure, calculate how long the projectile remains airborne and the distance it covers along the incline, using g = 10 m/s².
conditions: projectile launched horizontally from a point on the incline

figure.description: An inclined plane rises from the horizontal ground at an angle of 30°, marked at its base. Near the top of the incline, a horizontal velocity arrow of 20 m/s points to the left; the angle between this horizontal arrow and the incline surface is marked as 30°.

solution.approach: Use horizontal and vertical motion from the launch point and find when the fall matches the downward slope of the incline.

steps.text: Set up horizontal and vertical motion from the launch point, with the horizontal velocity constant and the vertical velocity starting from zero.
steps.equation: x = ut, y = −½gt² (taking down as negative)

steps.text: The incline drops at 30° below horizontal along the direction of motion, so the particle lands when the fall matches the incline's slope times the horizontal distance.
Solve for the time of flight.
Find the horizontal distance travelled in this time.
Divide by cos30° to get the distance measured along the incline; this gives the final answer.

final_answer.value: time of flight ≈ 2.31 s, range along the incline ≈ 53.33 m

common_mistakes.text: Reporting the horizontal distance of about 46.19 m as the range, instead of dividing by cos30° for the distance along the incline, gives a wrong value.
